title: Would you consider "Martyrs" (2008) to be an example of queer cinema?

commenti.body: Are the characters in the film actually queer? I watched the film for the first time within the past week and I do not remember there being any kind of queerness in the film. As a gay person who looks for queerness in everything, I do not remember seeing much in the film, though I would be down to listen to an argument for it.

The main female characters kiss on the lips when after they are done killing the people who were involved in their torture, which does very strongly imply they have a romantic relationship or at least very least, the one initiating the kiss is the one in love with her best friend.
Here's a image of them kissing: https://images.app.goo.gl/wHgrJk1eea1H3wvG6

I always read that scene as Anna having a romantic interest in Lucie deep down, but Lucie not really recuperating that feeling - so more like the second part of your comment. Lucie might not really be able to show that type of love and effection in general at that point, because of her trauma in her youth.

Is the film about the experience of queer people or are the characters simply queer? In my opinion that is a big difference. It should be normalized that some people are lgbtq+ and there are good arguments for including them in stories without having to tell specifically their stories.
But I think if you call it queer cinema specifically, the experience of being queer should be a major plot point. 

To make a point, girls kissing is sometimes used more in the exploitation and excitement sense, and this would not be queer cinema in my eyes. 

Case in point, The Wire has a very mature way of portraying a society in which some people happen to be queer, and their complicated stories are part of the overall story. But I would not call it a queer tv-series, because it is just one of many underlying scenes in the series and not its focus point.

Of course you can. You can read it anyway you like. That’s the beauty of criticism. From my perspective it’s not even a particularly tenuous reading. As you’ve show it’s supported by the text.

I hope I’ve hit the character limit.
